title: Sub-Scope Report List Filter Delivery
summary: deliver dual generated sub-scope manifests, focused metadata editing, public Concepts copy, shared title-prefix filtering, and Manage-only group controls
content_html:
Sub-Scope Report List Filter Delivery

Status And Order

Active as SSI-4, after Sub-Scope Package Preparation Delivery. SSI-4.0 and SSI-4.1 are accepted. SSI-4.1a absorbs first-class Tag Editor New Tag document creation into this delivery and is implemented at its review gate before generated projections continue.

SSI-4 gives public and Manage reports one generated-manifest loading model. Both receive shared title-prefix filtering. The Analysis Tags Manage manifest additionally carries document-owned group metadata for group-filter buttons.

SSI-4 does not widen SSI-2 Delete, SSI-3 package preparation, the Docs Viewer search subsystem, or Tag Registry ownership.

Complete Outcome

Every docs_subscope list offers a search-style input that filters its already loaded records by title prefix. Typing p shows titles beginning with p; typing pri narrows that result further.

The Manage report for { scope: analysis, sub_scope: tags } additionally offers All tags, subject, domain, form, and theme buttons with counts, matching the established group-filter treatment on Tag Registry. Public routes do not receive or render the group facet and present the collection as Concepts, not Tags.

Filtering is immediate and client-side over one loaded manifest:

public: manifest.json
        -> title-prefix filter

manage: manage-manifest.json
        -> title-prefix filter + optional document-group filter

It issues no search request, builds no search index, fetches no by-ID payload for matching, and does not make the child collection a separate search surface.

The projection architecture is documented in Sub-Scope Public And Manage Manifests.

Presentation Identity

The stable technical identity remains:

scope: analysis
sub_scope: tags

tags remains in source paths, manifest paths, URL/report parameters, service targets, configuration lookup, and Tag Editor integration. This delivery does not rename or alias that identity.

Presentation is route-specific:

Manage collection title: Tags
Public collection title: Concepts

The canonical sub-scope configuration owns both labels. The browser-config builder resolves the Manage label into the local config and the public label into the public config, so the shared report receives one already resolved title for its route. Report headings, loading/count/empty states, Back copy, filter labels, clear controls, and accessible names must use that resolved title. Shared runtime code must not hardcode tag or tags, or derive presentation copy from sub_scope.

The report-host document d-20260624-213316-478639 may safely change its source title, Markdown heading, and introductory copy from Tags to Concepts. Its doc_id, viewer_report, and viewer_report_subscope continue to own routing. Because the host document has one shared source, Concepts will also be its title in Manage Index, Recent, search, and rendered content. That accepted shared document title is independent of the Manage report collection label Tags.

Meaning Of Concept

tag remains the semantic-token kind and Tag Registry identity. Its resolver continues to follow the registry relationships:

text
  -> semantic token: tag
  -> Tag Registry tag
  -> work_id / series_id / doc_id

Concept names the additional editorial context represented by a linked document. When SSI-4.1a makes Tag Editor create a tag and its document in one transaction, the tag retains its registry identity while the document becomes its concept context. After creation, that document is canonical Docs Viewer content and may diverge from the originating tag.

This language introduces no concept semantic token, registry, identifier, resolver, relationship table, or route. The public report is called Concepts because it presents contextual documents rather than Tag Registry rows. A standalone sub-scope document can therefore also be presented as a concept without acquiring a Tag Registry identity.

Dual-Manifest Boundary

One sub-scope document build writes sibling projections from the same validated source snapshot.

The working publication manifest retains only viewable public-safe records:

{
  "docs": [
    {"doc_id": "<id>", "title": "<title>"}
  ]
}

Publish continues to copy that manifest to site/ unchanged.

The local Manage manifest contains every source document:

{
  "groups": ["subject", "domain", "form", "theme"],
  "docs": [
    {
      "doc_id": "<id>",
      "title": "<title>",
      "ui_status": "",
      "viewable": true,
      "group": "subject"
    }
  ]
}

groups is present only when the owning sub-scope config defines an ordered document-group vocabulary. group is optional on each document.

The builder writes the Manage projection to:

docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/sub-scopes/<sub-scope>/manage-manifest.json

Manage browser config points to that local file. Public browser config keeps pointing to the public-safe manifest. The publication gate must explicitly exclude the Manage manifest.

The shared report loads both through the same manifest path and normalization mechanism. The current source-backed GET /docs/sub-scope-documents override is retired as the report list source after an exact consumer audit. It must not remain as a silent fallback.

Document Group Ownership

Analysis Tags documents gain one optional scalar front-matter field:

group: subject

The configured allowed values are:

subject
domain
form
theme

The Analysis tags sub-scope config owns those values and their display order. Blank is valid and removes the field.

group is Docs Viewer document metadata:

  • the source model reads and validates it;
  • the focused sub-scope Edit metadata workflow hydrates it and presents the configured values;
  • metadata save writes or removes it through the exact { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } target;
  • the ordinary targeted sub-scope build updates the Manage manifest and local detail payloads; and
  • the public manifest and public detail projection omit it.

The metadata workflow rejects an array, an unknown value, or group on a collection that has no configured document groups. Parent-document metadata behavior remains unchanged. Group-only and status-only writes follow the existing recent-edit rule: they change the source revision but do not advance last_updated. Title, summary, or body changes continue to advance it.

Metadata Editing Boundary

Sub-scope documents use a focused metadata editor rather than adding sub-scope-only switches and fields to the ordinary document modal.

The Analysis Tags recipe contains the metadata valid for those documents, including group, and has no document-parent control. Its effective ui_status choices are resolved for the exact sub-scope from Docs Viewer configuration and returned with the metadata read; the editor does not assume the ordinary-document status list. Analysis Tags may initially configure the same values deliberately, while retaining independent ownership and the ability to diverge later.

This is a UI and metadata-contract boundary, not a duplicate persistence path. The ordinary and sub-scope editors reuse the exact-target metadata read/write transport, field controls where suitable, revision protection, source mutation, and rebuild transaction. The service validates the fields and choices allowed for { scope, sub_scope }; hiding a control in the browser is not the authorization boundary.

SSI-4 does not introduce an arbitrary schema-driven form framework or a second sub-scope metadata endpoint. The focused workflow belongs here because document-owned group must be editable before the Manage report can filter its generated projection.

No Tag Registry Synchronization

doc.group and tag.group are independent canonical fields in different domains.

A one-time migration may use the current Tag Registry relationship to seed the 245 generated Analysis Tag documents:

tag_registry row --doc_id--> generated document
tag.group        --seed once--> doc.group

The three pre-existing independent documents remain without group so their classification can be chosen explicitly through Docs Viewer later.

The Tag Editor New Tag path makes Registry and document creation one first-class transaction. The new document receives its initial group from the new tag and the new Registry row receives its immutable doc_id.

These are two create-only seed paths, not synchronization:

  • the migration initializes the 245 existing generated documents once; and
  • SSI-4.1a makes each future tag creation initialize its new document once.

After an Analysis Tag document exists:

  • ordinary document builds do not read Tag Registry;
  • later Tag Editor edits do not mutate document group or trigger a Docs Viewer build for that purpose;
  • Docs Viewer does not compare, repair, or synchronize the two fields;
  • a later tag.group change leaves doc.group unchanged; and
  • neither seed path overwrites an existing document or becomes a repair or synchronization path.

A document that does not fit one group can remain ungrouped and appears under All tags. Multiple document groups are not introduced by this delivery.

Matching And Facet Semantics

The report retains the complete loaded manifest as source state and derives a visible row projection from it.

  • Search matches the normalized displayed title only.
  • Matching is case-insensitive and requires the whole title to begin with the normalized query.
  • doc_id, status, viewability, group, body content, other metadata, and rendered detail HTML are not text-search inputs.
  • An empty query shows every row allowed by the active group.
  • All tags removes only the group constraint; it does not clear the query.
  • Choosing a group preserves the query and shows the intersection of both filters.
  • Clearing the search preserves the active group.
  • Group-button counts describe the complete Manage manifest: All tags counts every document, while each group counts documents carrying that document-owned value.
  • Ungrouped documents appear only under All tags.
  • The list status distinguishes visible matches from the complete loaded collection and provides a contained no-match state.

Report State

  • Filter state belongs to one mounted { scope, sub_scope } report instance.
  • Opening a filtered row and returning to the same list preserves the query and active group.
  • Changing collection or unmounting the report clears it.
  • Filtering does not add URL state or change subdoc.
  • Detail validation continues to use the complete loaded manifest, not only currently visible rows.
  • Public collections have no active group state or group controls.

Selection Interaction

SSI-4 follows SSI-3 so filtering must compose with collection selection:

  • filtering never silently checks, unchecks, or prunes IDs;
  • checked IDs remain the only package-action target even when a checked row is filtered out;
  • Select all replaces the checked set with every currently visible eligible row after applying both filters, clearing checked IDs excluded by either filter; and
  • Clear still clears the complete collection selection.

These rules keep filtering presentational and prevent a query from broadening or silently changing a mutation/export target.

In Scope

  • Optional scalar document group metadata for configured sub-scopes.
  • A focused sub-scope Edit metadata workflow, including Analysis Tags group and target-specific status choices.
  • First-class Tag Editor New Tag creation of one linked Analysis Tag document and Registry row in SSI-4.1a.
  • One-time group seeding for the 245 generated tag documents.
  • Sibling public-safe and Manage manifests from one document build.
  • Manage report cutover from the source-backed inventory to its generated manifest.
  • One accessible title-prefix input in the shared report.
  • Route-resolved Tags Manage copy and Concepts public copy without changing the tags technical identity.
  • Preservation of tag as the semantic-token and registry identity; concept remains a document presentation/content role only.
  • Optional group buttons derived only from Manage-manifest data.
  • Matching/total count, clear, empty, no-match, detail-return, remount, and selection composition.
  • Focused source-model, metadata, builder, publication, pure-filter, report-module, public-isolation, and realistic-list evidence.

Not In Scope

  • Tag Registry reads during ordinary document build or report runtime.
  • Synchronizing, comparing, or repairing doc.group from tag.group.
  • Triggering Docs Viewer builds from later Tag Editor group changes.
  • Renaming or aliasing the tags sub-scope identity, routes, paths, manifests, targets, or Tag Editor contracts.
  • A concept semantic token, registry, ID, resolver, or relationship model.
  • Separate public and Manage report implementations.
  • Publishing manage-manifest.json, group values, or group controls.
  • Multiple document groups or a generic configurable facet framework.
  • A generic metadata-form schema engine, duplicate metadata endpoints, or a redesign of the ordinary document metadata editor.
  • Docs Viewer overall search or build_search.py.
  • A sub-scope-specific search index, endpoint, route, or results page.
  • Full-text body search or eager by-ID loading.
  • doc_id, substring, token-anywhere, fuzzy, or rendered-content matching.
  • Server-side pagination, ranking, highlighting, or saved queries.
  • Filtering the parent Index, Recent, scope selector, or another report type.

Delivery Tracker

[x] SSI-4.0 — Freeze Ownership And Filter Semantics

  • [x] Keep the public manifest minimal and add one sibling generated Manage manifest.
  • [x] Make optional group canonical Docs Viewer document metadata.
  • [x] Keep the four allowed document groups in Analysis Tags sub-scope config.
  • [x] Limit Tag Registry use to a one-time seed for 245 generated documents.
  • [x] Leave the three independent documents ungrouped.
  • [x] Keep tags as technical identity while public presentation uses Concepts and Manage presentation uses Tags.
  • [x] Keep tag as the semantic-token/registry identity and define concept only as the contextual document role.
  • [x] Freeze title-only prefix, group intersection, count, clear, no-match, and Select all behavior.

Evidence:

  • The current local and public Analysis Tags manifests contain the same 248 minimal { doc_id, title } records.
  • The current Manage report substitutes a live source inventory for its local manifest; the accepted target replaces that exception with a sibling generated Manage manifest.
  • Tag Registry has 245 linked rows; three Analysis Tag documents are independent.
  • The accepted ownership model permits doc.group and tag.group to diverge after one explicit seed.
  • The current config projects one title: Tags into both routes; the accepted target resolves separate public and Manage labels during browser-config generation.
  • The accepted terminology does not add a second semantic-reference kind or duplicate Tag Registry identity.
  • The accepted matching model follows prefix behavior but uses displayed document title rather than tag ID.

Review gate: accepted. Code delivery begins with document metadata; no runtime filtering edits belong in SSI-4.0.

[x] SSI-4.1 — Add Sub-Scope Metadata Workflow And Document Group

  • [x] Configure ordered optional groups for the Analysis tags sub-scope.
  • [x] Extend source parsing and validation with one optional scalar group.
  • [x] Resolve the effective ui_status vocabulary per sub-scope and return it, with group choices, through the exact metadata read.
  • [x] Add a focused sub-scope Edit metadata editor for valid Analysis Tags fields, including group, with no document-parent control.
  • [x] Reuse the shared exact-target save, revision, mutation, and rebuild transaction rather than duplicating the ordinary workflow.
  • [x] Reject document-parent writes, arrays, unknown group or status values, and unconfigured group writes without changing source.
  • [x] Freeze and test group-only revision and last_updated behavior.

Evidence:

  • Analysis tags now owns ten ordered status values and the four ordered document groups in canonical scope configuration.
  • Metadata reads return the exact { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } record, configured choices, and a SHA-256 source revision. Saves require that receipt and return HTTP 409 when it is stale.
  • Source and builder validation reject array, unknown, and unconfigured group values. Public manifest and by-ID payload shapes remain group-free.
  • Group-only writes preserve last_updated under the existing recent-edit rule while returning the new source revision.
  • An Analysis tags dry run validated all 248 current sources with zero warnings and no generated-output diff.
  • Focused Python evidence: 66 tests passed across scope config, target resolution, mutations, metadata integration, and sub-scope builds.
  • The existing 11-test sub-scope delete revision suite also passed after the shared conflict payload was generalized for metadata saves.
  • Browser evidence: the module focus smoke and standalone Manage-route smoke passed. A rendered check on the real ordered Analysis Tag document showed only title, summary, date, date display, status, group, and non-viewable; Parent was hidden and disabled; status and group options matched configuration exactly. The modal was cancelled without a source write.

Review gate: focused source/service evidence and a manual check of the dedicated sub-scope editor prove document-only ownership, exact status/group choices, and the absence of a parent control before generated projection work.

Ready for review. Stop here before SSI-4.1a.

[x] SSI-4.1a — Wire First-Class New Tag Document Creation

  • [x] Extend New Tag to allocate one immutable document ID and create the exact Analysis tags source document alongside the Tag Registry row.
  • [x] Seed the document title, description, and initial scalar group; record its doc_id in the new Registry row.
  • [x] Keep the operation create-only: refuse an existing Registry identity, existing destination document, or partial overwrite.
  • [x] Make Registry and Markdown creation atomic or explicitly compensated on rebuild/write failure.
  • [x] Rebuild the Analysis tags projection after successful creation and return one truthful UI/activity result.
  • [x] Keep later Edit Tag saves independent: no document update, comparison, repair, or synchronization path.
  • [x] Prove existing Registry rows and Analysis Tag documents are untouched by focused success and failure evidence.

Review gate: one realistic New Tag transaction proves that Registry and document identities wire together once, then remain independently editable.

Ready for review. Stop here before SSI-4.2.

SSI-4.1a Evidence

  • New Tag now plans one immutable doc_id, appends one Registry v4 row, creates the exact configured Analysis tags Markdown source, and runs the confined child builder. The source seeds title, description, scalar group, and normal document metadata without reintroducing the retired body group marker.
  • The commit is guarded against stale Registry bytes and existing destinations. A Registry write failure removes only the just-created source. A child build failure restores the exact original Registry bytes, removes only the exact created source, reruns the same child build, and returns source_restored, recovery_rebuild, and retry_safe instead of success.
  • A temporary configured Analysis tags transaction drove the real child builder and produced the new manifest/by-ID payload while retaining the existing Registry row and sibling source byte-for-byte. Focused failure fixtures proved existing-destination refusal and compensated build failure.
  • The real current source inventory passed a write-free create plan with 245 uniquely linked Registry rows and 248 direct child documents. No real tag or document was created.
  • Registry patch mode no longer offers the invalid Registry-only New Tag fragment. Its retained manual fallback now prepares the linked row, exact Markdown destination/content, create-only guards, and child rebuild command together, while stating that nothing was written. Server results and activity detail name the tag and linked document. Existing Edit Tag code remains Registry-only and unchanged.
  • Focused Python evidence passed 30 tests across creation, Registry mutation, route response, activity, and the prior bootstrap. The sub-scope builder suite passed 8 tests. Explicit Python/JavaScript lint and git diff --check passed.
  • Maintained studio-tag-smoke passed all 11 commands, including local create API/activity and browser module request/result boundaries. Run evidence: var/admin/test-runs/ssi-4-1a-gate/summary.md.

[ ] SSI-4.2 — Generate Dual Manifests

  • [ ] Build manifest.json and manage-manifest.json from one validated source snapshot and deterministic order.
  • [ ] Keep the public manifest at viewable { doc_id, title }.
  • [ ] Put all documents, configured group order, status, viewability, and optional document group in the Manage manifest.
  • [ ] Project Tags into Manage browser config and Concepts into public browser config from the canonical sub-scope presentation settings.
  • [ ] Point Manage browser config to the Manage manifest.
  • [ ] Exclude the Manage manifest from public projection preview/apply and validate its absence from site/.
  • [ ] Preserve existing by-ID generation and exact detail validation.

Review gate: builder and publication evidence proves the sibling projections are directly inspectable and public output is unchanged.

[ ] SSI-4.3 — Seed And Cut Over Manage

  • [ ] Preview one exact 245-document front-matter seed from the frozen current Tag Registry relationships.
  • [ ] Apply only absent group fields to those generated documents; leave the three independent sources unchanged.
  • [ ] Retire the generated documents' old body-only bold group marker when seeding front matter so later document edits cannot leave a stale visible duplicate.
  • [ ] Rebuild and reconcile source, Manage-manifest, and public-manifest inventories.
  • [ ] Switch the Manage report to normal manifest loading.
  • [ ] Audit and retire the source-backed inventory as a report list source, including client/config/tests with no remaining consumer.
  • [ ] Prove later Tag Registry group changes have no Docs Viewer mutation or build path.

Review gate: inspect the seed preview and resulting manifests before shared report filtering edits.

[ ] SSI-4.4 — Add Shared Report Filtering

  • [ ] Change the shared report-host document title, heading, and introductory copy to Concepts without changing its report identity fields.
  • [ ] Add the accessible title-prefix control and pure visible-row projection to docs_subscope.
  • [ ] Derive all route-visible report copy from the resolved sub-scope title; render Tags in Manage, Concepts in public, and no hardcoded tags copy in the shared report.
  • [ ] Render optional ordered group controls only when the loaded manifest provides them.
  • [ ] Compose title and group constraints without either control clearing the other.
  • [ ] Preserve the complete loaded manifest for validation and selection.
  • [ ] Preserve query and active group across detail and Back within one mounted collection.
  • [ ] Render truthful counts and contained empty/no-match states.
  • [ ] Keep public title filtering on the same shared implementation while public manifests provide no groups.

Review gate: module evidence proves filtering performs no new read, by-ID fetch, search import, or management import.

[ ] SSI-4.5 — Integration And Closeout

  • [ ] Verify filtering with contribution rows and selection controls.
  • [ ] Verify Select all includes every eligible row visible after both filters and no filtered-out ID.
  • [ ] Confirm public payloads, imports, requests, and UI remain group-free.
  • [ ] Confirm public report chrome says Concepts, Manage report chrome says Tags, and both still target sub_scope: tags.
  • [ ] Review ordinary, narrow, keyboard, prefix, clear, no-match, group, ungrouped, non-viewable, detail-return, and filtered-selection behavior.
  • [ ] Run the focused service, builder, report, and maintained Docs Viewer integration checks.
  • [ ] Record untested scale and tactile surfaces.
  • [ ] Update current-state architecture docs and close SSI-4 only after the Manage inventory exception is removed or explicitly retained for another named consumer.

Completion Gate

SSI-4 is complete only when one document build produces directly inspectable public and Manage list manifests, document group is independently editable through Docs Viewer, public and Manage users can filter titles by prefix, Manage can additionally filter Analysis Tags by document-owned group, and no runtime/build synchronization with Tag Registry or public group projection exists. New Tag Editor tags still bootstrap one initially grouped document, after which tag and document metadata may diverge.
